\section[entretanto]{entretanto — meanwhile, in the meantime; however}

\label{lesson:PT-C270-entretanto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for later, then the Portuguese for finally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: entretanto}
\textbf{entretanto} — \textquotedblleft{}meanwhile, in the meantime; however\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Eu fiz o jantar; entretanto, o meu irmão pôs a mesa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I made dinner; meanwhile my brother set out the plates and glasses.}
\end{quote}

In formal writing it can also mean ‘however’; in Brazil that is the main sense.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{entretanto} joins \emph{entre} \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{} and \emph{tanto} \textquotedblleft{}so much\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{inter} \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{} and \emph{tantum} \textquotedblleft{}so much\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): the time in between.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[simultaneamente]{simultaneamente — simultaneously, at the same time}

\label{lesson:PT-C270-simultaneamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for finally, then the Portuguese for meanwhile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: simultaneamente}
\textbf{simultaneamente} — \textquotedblleft{}simultaneously, at the same time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os dois telefones tocaram simultaneamente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The two phones rang at the same time.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{simultâneo}, ‘happening together’.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{simultaneamente} is built on \emph{simultâneo}, a learned word from Medieval Latin \emph{simultāneus}, which rests on Latin \emph{simul} \textquotedblleft{}at the same time, together\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[assim que]{assim que — as soon as}

\label{lesson:PT-C270-assim-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for meanwhile, then the Portuguese for simultaneously.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: assim que}
\textbf{assim que} — \textquotedblleft{}as soon as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Assim que cheguei a casa, começou a chover.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{As soon as I got home, it started to rain.}
\end{quote}

Joins two events that follow each other at once. About the future it takes the subjunctive: \emph{assim que puderes}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{assim} is usually traced to Latin \emph{ad sīc} \textquotedblleft{}so, in this way\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists it beside Spanish \emph{así}, from Latin \emph{sīc} \textquotedblleft{}so, thus\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[logo que]{logo que — the moment that, as soon as (formal)}

\label{lesson:PT-C270-logo-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for simultaneously, then the Portuguese for as soon as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: logo que}
\textbf{logo que} — \textquotedblleft{}the moment that, as soon as (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Logo que o filme acabou, as pessoas saíram.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The moment the film ended, people left.}
\end{quote}

A little more formal than \emph{assim que}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{logo} is inherited from Latin \emph{locō} \textquotedblleft{}in the place, on the spot\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{locus} \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}: on the spot, at once.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[subitamente]{subitamente — suddenly}

\label{lesson:PT-C270-subitamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for as soon as, then the Portuguese for the moment that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: subitamente}
\textbf{subitamente} — \textquotedblleft{}suddenly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Subitamente, as luzes apagaram-se.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Suddenly the lights went out.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{de repente}; storytellers like it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{subitamente} is built on \emph{súbito} \textquotedblleft{}sudden\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{subitus} \textquotedblleft{}sudden, unexpected\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the adverb ending \emph{-mente}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
